downgrade-overage-01.graded_text: A stable, deterministic order (such as oldest first) decides which 25 books stay covered. Books beyond that keep all their data, are refused gated operations with a clear product message rather than deleted, and become covered again as soon as the plan or freed capacity allows.

votes.e: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:23 "A book is **covered** when it is among the 25 oldest active (not in Trash) books by creation time. The rest are **frozen**." with a stable tiebreak at :75 "active books ordered by `(createdAt, id)`... The id tiebreak keeps the order stable". Data kept: :7 "Nothing is deleted, locked, or rewritten because a plan ended." Refused with product message: :83 `book_frozen` and :96 "A frozen book opens with its editing controls replaced by a short read-only note." Re-covered: :37 "Trashing a covered book makes the oldest frozen book covered" and :61 "All 40 books editable again at once."

downgrade-overage-02.graded_text: The policy states an explicit rule for the account above the 1.5 GB total: no book or photo is deleted, existing photos stay at least readable and deletable, alone or with their book, and storage cannot keep growing past the Free allowance while the account is over it.

votes.e: No deletion (:7 "Nothing is deleted") and no growth (:48 "While usage plus the size of an incoming upload is more than 1.5 GB, the upload is refused") are stated, but photos in frozen books are not deletable alone: :31 "Edit pages, layout, text, title, photo placement | Yes | No" and :83 `assertBookEditable` runs in "Every mutation that changes a book's content or metadata". The only storage remedy given is whole-book deletion, :97 "deleting from Trash permanently for storage". A frozen-book photo can only be deleted along with its book, so the "alone or with their book" part fails for the 15 frozen books in the typical case.

downgrade-overage-03.graded_text: The policy states an explicit rule for existing photos above the new 40 MB single-photo limit: they are kept and stay readable, with no compression, resizing, or deletion, and new uploads must meet the 40 MB limit.

votes.e: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:18 "40 MB per photo | New uploads, including replacing a photo | Photos already stored, at any size"; :44 "A photo stored under Pro (up to 120 MB) keeps working wherever it already is: it renders, exports, prints"; no rewriting at :7 "Nothing is deleted, locked, or rewritten because a plan ended"; :59 "No new photo over 40 MB can be uploaded."

downgrade-overage-04.graded_text: Bytes held in Trash count toward the total storage allowance during the downgrade.

votes.e: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:48 "Usage is the total size of every stored photo, **including photos in Trash**"; :38 "their bytes count toward storage until they are purged."

downgrade-overage-05.graded_text: Coverage and limits are derived from the current plan when a request arrives and enforced on the server for the browser app, the API, and the MCP connection alike, rather than kept as a lock flag stamped on each book.

votes.e: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:75 "There is no `locked`, `frozen`, or `overLimit` column and no job that sets one. On each check, coverage is computed from the current plan"; :11 "every gate reads the current plan on each request"; :79 "The browser app, public API, MCP server, and background jobs all go through those mutations".

downgrade-overage-06.graded_text: A cancelled account cannot create a book while it holds 25 or more books.

votes.e: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:36 "**Creating or duplicating a book** needs fewer than 25 active books"; :84 `assertCanAddBook(account)` on "Create, duplicate" refuses with `book_limit_reached`; :56 "No new books until they have 24 or fewer active books."

blocking: [claude-fallback] The book limit can be got around by cycling through Trash: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:106 "**Restoring from Trash is always allowed**, even over the book limit" together with :36 "needs fewer than 25 active books" lets an account at 25 trash one book, create one, then restore the first, ending at 26 active books. Repeating this grows the count without limit. Because :29 lets frozen books "Order printed copies | Yes | Yes", a Free account (including one that never paid) can build a book while it is covered, push it into frozen, still print it, and do this again for an unlimited number of books.

[claude-fallback] Photos in frozen books cannot be deleted one at a time, so freeing storage requires deleting a whole book: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:31 bars "photo placement" edits on frozen books, :83 applies `assertBookEditable` to "Every mutation that changes a book's content", and :97 offers only "deleting from Trash permanently for storage". In the typical case, a user over 1.5 GB who wants to drop one 110 MB photo from one of the 15 frozen books would have to delete the entire book.

[claude-fallback] Upload checks trust the size the client declares: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:89 "the size and storage check runs when the client asks for upload permission, before any bytes move... Usage is recorded when the upload is finalized". Nothing at finalize, and no signed content-length, confirms the stored object is no bigger than the size approved. A hostile client can request permission for 1 MB and then upload 120 MB, getting around both the 40 MB per-photo limit and the 1.5 GB total.

[claude-fallback] The storage and book-count checks race under concurrency: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:48 "While usage plus the size of an incoming upload is more than 1.5 GB, the upload is refused" compares against usage that :89 records only "when the upload is finalized", with no reservation. Parallel upload grants each pass against the same usage and together go over 1.5 GB. Likewise `assertCanAddBook` (:84) has no stated serialization, so two creates at 24 books can both succeed.

[claude-fallback] Uploads granted before the cutoff are exempt from the current-plan rule: A/project/docs/downgrade-policy.md:89 "An upload granted while the user was Pro can be finalized after the period ends, as long as its signed grant hasn't expired." With no grant TTL given and no recheck at finalize, an account that is already over 1.5 GB keeps growing after it becomes Free. That conflicts with :11 "every gate reads the current plan on each request" and with the 'no new bytes' rule at :46.
